title: Reading
summary: The agent can read all of the app's data, with SQL that can't write.
description: The app's data is its SQLite database, and whatever the product keeps beside it. The more of it the agent can read, the better it answers, so it reads freely; what keeps the data safe is that reading can't change it.

requirements.text: The agent can run SQL on the app's SQLite database, on a connection opened read-only, so no statement it runs can change the data.
A query runs only if it is one statement that reads; any other is refused, and the agent is told why.
A query returns at most `counsel.query-rows` rows and is stopped after `counsel.query-timeout`, and the agent is told when a result was cut short.
The agent can list the tables and views it can read, with their columns and types.
The product describes what each table the agent can read holds, and each column whose meaning or unit its name doesn't make plain, and the agent is given these descriptions.
Tables the product marks as hidden, such as the bookkeeping of a device, are neither listed to the agent nor readable by it.
Data the product keeps outside its database, the agent reads through read tools the product gives it.
Each message the user sends tells the agent what the user has open in the app: the screen, and the item on it.
Each query the agent runs shows in the chat, folded, with its SQL and how many rows it returned; unfolded, it shows the rows.

values.description: The most rows one query returns to the agent.
How long one query may run.
